registry_policy.default_model_policy_note: Apply these defaults to future mainline, visible department, automation, business dispatch, and disposable sub-agent calls when the native tool/runtime accepts explicit settings. Do not send no-op turns only to mutate settings on healthy existing threads. Dead-thread recovery no-op probes should omit settings overrides unless specifically testing settings update.
registry_policy.note: Only thread IDs listed with status=active_visible are dispatchable. If an old thread ID is absent from this registry and cannot be found in the current visible thread scan, treat it as gone instead of maintaining a separate blacklist.
registry_policy.r2_failover_note: For MWORKS/ROS2/UE, R2 may receive explicit PMO or legacy ops patrol packets for source_static, diagnostic_only, packet_contract_fix, rule_sync_only, or checker/review work when R1 is dead, stale, or blocked and a safe task is available. R2 must not run live MWORKS, live ROS2/RViz/FAST-LIO, UE runtime/build/editor, GUI clicks, login/authorization/save/restart actions, or setpoint publication under this default failover rule.
registry_policy.r3_failover_note: User approved creation of MWORKS/ROS2/UE R3 reserve threads on 2026-06-09. R3 threads are active_visible reserve routes for explicit PMO or legacy ops patrol packets only. PMO proposes or approves R3 only after R2 failover still leaves a P0 partition idle or blocked long enough that reserve static/diagnostic/checker/review capacity is useful. Do not trigger R3 merely because R1/R2 had repeated dead-thread incidents within 24 hours. R3 must not run live MWORKS/ROS2/UE runtime or GUI/editor/build tasks by default.
